events.title: The third mark beside a birth
events.body: On the same page Cailean finds the birth of Aisling entered with a mark he has seen only three or four times in a year of copying, never explained in any book given him, and recognises it for the mark the camps' whisper had already fixed to one child in the settlement.

events.title: Cailean walks to Tobar dhìreach
events.body: Rather than report to the cellar, Cailean walks the hill road to Tobar dhìreach with the seven names copied onto a scrap of paper inside his coat, to ask whether a line so old could truly be Donnchadh's own.

events.title: A custodian of Cill ghlas answers the Company's agent
events.body: Asked by a Company agent whether she knows of any coal-touched child in her district, a custodian of Cill ghlas answers that she keeps no roll of miracles, only of births and deaths, and that the office is welcome to search her books for either.

events.title: Peigi Ghlas dies at Cill ghlas
events.body: Peigi Ghlas dies at Cill ghlas, her petition still unanswered, having trimmed Brìde's lamp herself the week before her death and said that she had asked the Residency once and meant to leave the asking there.

events.title: Ruth Pallant teaches Hannah Webb the night watch
events.body: At Ceann mhòr, an old net-mender named Ruth Pallant tells the field-worker Hannah Webb of a night watch her own people's fisher-forebears learned from the island folk, kept in silence under a grey goose said to hold the sea shut. Hannah carries the telling of it home to the concession.

events.title: Hannah Webb's first vigil
events.body: In a field behind her landlord's byre near Baile chrom, Hannah Webb keeps the silent watch for the first time, and sees, or believes she sees, a pale shape cross the night sky before she sleeps through a whole night for the first time in ten years on the island.

events.title: The watch spreads along the concession's edge
events.body: Word of Hannah Webb's night vigil passes among the human labourers of the concession after a field hand sees her keeping it. Within a season a handful of others try it, and by autumn six or seven keep the field together on clear nights, spaced apart and silent.

events.title: The berth toll and the docker Tòmas Ruadh
events.body: The Company posts a new toll on every ton loaded at the Ros dhomhain coal berths. The docker Tòmas Ruadh, whom Daniel Webb once pulled clear of a falling beam, tells him of it, and the two speak for the first time of standing off the hooks together.

events.title: Raghnall Breac walks to Cill ghlas
events.body: With his knees gone stiff for the low work at Baile thais and two grandchildren to feed, the ageing hewer Raghnall Breac walks two days to the new galleries at Cill ghlas, where the pay is better and the headings still stand tall enough for a man to work upright. He writes to his daughter Eilidh twice a year.

events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill given a seat at the Lamp-Watch's table
events.body: The crew-leader Eilidh nic Raghnaill of Baile thais is asked, for the first time, to sit at the table where the Lamp-Watch keeps its business, and copies its minutes into a second book kept in her own linen chest, where no Company clerk would think to look.

events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill at the fenced ground
events.body: Eilidh nic Raghnaill walks to Cill ghlas to find her father's grave and finds instead the fence and the fallen headgear of the eighth heading. A constable turns her away from the closed ground. She writes nothing of the hour in the Lamp-Watch's book.

events.title: Fionnlagh's warning at Muileann chrom
events.body: The overseer Fionnlagh tells the new agent Edgar Holt that the flooded ground under one heading at Muileann chrom has never gone a night without its pumps, drawing as it does from an unmapped old working above it. Holt orders the pumps stopped regardless, to spare coal for the winding-gear until a delayed barge arrives.
